findings.claim: With the default path (the current directory) in a repository root that holds no .okf/, resolve_target opens a namespace named '.' that covers the whole repository (store .kmaudit/..sqlite). Every later path then narrows it, so `kmaudit claims todo docs` reports namespace '.' and never gets its own store. That is the clash the ticket exists to prevent, and the old code refused this case.

The first open of the .okf namespace from a legacy store is not safe when several processes run it at once. Every process copies into the same .okf.partial and then renames it over .okf.sqlite, possibly under a process that already has the file open. Six parallel `kmaudit claims list .okf` runs on a copy of the real store: 5 of 6 exit 1 with 'disk I/O error' in each of 5 trials. The store docstring promises that parallel agents can work at once.

The r2b command (-k maps) selects only test_a_path_inside_a_namespace_maps_to_it. The refusal half of the row, a parent of an existing namespace exits 1 naming it, is tested by test_a_folder_holding_a_namespace_is_refused_naming_it, but the row's command never runs that test.

r1 says todo hands out a section for every heading of every .md file, but test_plain_folder_hands_out_every_page compares only the set of concepts. A dropped section inside a file (guide.md has two) would still pass.
